title: Filamin-A links transcriptional disruption to dopaminergic decline in progressive supranuclear palsy
title_zh: Filamin-A连接转录紊乱与进行性上行性麻痹中多巴胺衰退
abstract: Abstract Progressive supranuclear palsy is a late-onset neurodegenerative disorder characterized by tau aggregation and prominent dopaminergic dysfunction, yet the upstream molecular processes linking transcriptional abnormalities to dopaminergic failure remain poorly understood. To explore these mechanisms, we performed an integrated multi-omics analysis using a mouse model with overexpression of human filamin-A, a cytoskeletal protein genetically implicated in progressive supranuclear palsy. Analyses were conducted in young adult mice (5–7 months) and aged mice (14–16 months) of both sexes, with transcriptomic, epigenomic, biochemical, metabolomic and behavioural profiling performed across multiple brain regions. In parallel, post-mortem human brain tissue from 11 individuals with progressive supranuclear palsy and five neurologically normal controls was analysed for biochemical validation using samples from the frontal cortex and striatum. Transcriptomic profiling identified immediate early gene-centred transcriptional dysregulation as a prominent and early molecular alteration. This change, accompanied by chromatin accessibility alterations, was associated with the activation of activator protein 1-dependent gene programmes and region-specific changes in dopaminergic protein markers across the cortex, striatum and midbrain. Multi-layered analyses revealed cortical monoamine depletion together with early striatal dopaminergic sensitization, indicating a close association between immediate early gene dysregulation and dopaminergic circuit imbalance. With ageing, the coupling was lost, coinciding with dopaminergic exhaustion and deficits in locomotor, cognitive and social behaviours. In human analyses, post-mortem brain samples from individuals with progressive supranuclear palsy showed reduced dopamine D2 receptor expression compared with neurologically normal controls, together with region-dependent alterations in c-Fos expression and enrichment of activator protein 1-related motifs in regions with reduced chromatin accessibility. Together, these findings suggest that filamin-A-dependent cytoskeletal stress acts as an upstream molecular context in which immediate early gene-centred transcriptional dysregulation emerges and becomes linked to dopaminergic vulnerability in progressive supranuclear palsy.
abstract_zh: 摘要 进行性上行性麻痹是一种晚发性神经退行性疾病，其特征是tau蛋白聚集和明显的多巴胺功能障碍，但导致转录异常与多巴胺功能衰退的上游分子机制尚不清楚。为探索这些机制，我们利用转基因小鼠模型进行了综合多组学分析，该模型表达人Filamin-A，这是一种与进行性上行性麻痹遗传相关的细胞骨架蛋白。研究分别在5-7个月（年轻）和14-16个月（老年）的两性小鼠中进行，涉及多脑区的转录组、表观组、生化、代谢组和行为表型分析。同时，利用11例进行性上行性麻痹患者和5例神经学正常对照的尸检脑组织，通过前额叶皮质和纹状体样本进行生化验证。转录组分析确定了即刻早期基因为中心的转录紊乱作为一种突出且早期的分子改变。这一变化伴随着染色质可及性的改变，与 activator protein 1（AP-1）依赖性基因程序的激活以及皮质、纹状体和中脑中多巴胺蛋白标志物的区域特异性变化相关。多层次分析揭示了皮质单胺耗竭与纹状体早期多巴胺敏感化之间的紧密关联，表明即刻早期基因紊乱与多巴胺电路失衡密切相关。随着年龄增长，这种耦合关系丧失，伴随多巴胺耗竭和运动、认知和社交行为缺陷。在人类分析中，进行性上行性麻痹患者的尸检脑组织显示与神经学正常对照相比，多巴胺D2受体表达减少，且区域依赖性的c-Fos表达改变，以及在染色质可及性减少的区域中富集了 activator protein 1相关基序。综上所述，这些发现表明，Filamin-A依赖的细胞骨架应激是即刻早期基因中心转录紊乱出现并与进行性上行性麻痹中多巴胺脆弱性相关联的上游分子背景。
